models.name: Bolex Stereo
models.summary: A 3-D attachment for the non-reflex H-series, recording both eyes on one strip of ordinary 16mm film. Twin rear lenses sit 5.3 mm apart and a prism block widens that to an interocular of 64 mm, close to the average human spacing. f/2.8, no focusing: it is set at the hyperfocal distance for about 10 ft and left there. The matching 20 mm projection lens carries polarising filters at 135 and 45 degrees, so showing the results needs polarised glasses and a silver screen. US$397.50 in 1952, which was more than most of the cameras it bolted onto.

sources.title: Hess, Hillary (2024). "Bolex Stereo", in James Layton (ed.), Film Atlas
sources.note: Published by FIAF, Brussels, and the George Eastman Museum, Rochester. Read in full, November 2026, and the source of every figure above. The entry states no licence, so it is cited rather than reproduced and the wording here is this archive's own.

sources.title: Fits the non-reflex Bolex only
sources.note: The reflex prism of an H-16 Rex occupies the space the attachment's own optics need. Anyone matching one to a camera should check which they have before buying.

sources.title: Still wanted
sources.note: Pacific Rim Camera lists a "Bolex Sterero Instruction Book" (their spelling), which would be Paillard's own account of the system. Not yet read. The end of production is also unsettled: about 1954 is the Film Atlas reading, and how many were sold at that price is not recorded anywhere found so far.
